conventions.basis_order: the C(n,r) r-subsets of E in COLEX order: A < B iff max(A xor B) in B; equivalently sort each ascending r-tuple by its reversal.  Index j runs 0..M-1.
conventions.chirotope: a uniform chirotope chi is evaluated on ascending r-tuples and takes values in {+1,-1}; it is valid iff every three-term Grassmann-Pluecker condition holds: for every (r-2)-subset L and every a<b<c<d disjoint from L, the three terms chi(L,a,b)chi(L,c,d), -chi(L,a,c)chi(L,b,d), chi(L,a,d)chi(L,b,c) are not all equal.
conventions.key_encoding: key is a 126-bit unsigned integer with bit (M-1-j) equal to 1 iff chi(B_j) = +1, B_j the j-th basis in colex order.  So the most significant bit is basis 0 and integer order on keys is lexicographic order on the sign string '+' > '-'.  Stored split as key = key_hi*2^64 + key_lo.
conventions.group: G' = S_n x {0,1}^n x {0,1} acting on the left by ((sig,eps,s).chi)(x_1..x_r) = (-1)^s (-1)^{|eps cap {x_1..x_r}|} chi(sig^{-1}x_1,..,sig^{-1}x_r).  |G'| = n! 2^(n+1).  The recorded stab is the order of the stabilizer of chi in G' (which contains the 2^kappa elements acting trivially on every chirotope; here kappa = 1, so the minimum is 2).
conventions.canonical_form: IMPORTANT -- the keys are extremal in their orbit under a COLOUR-RESTRICTED relabelling set, not under all of S_n.  Precisely: (1) call a basis MUTABLE if flipping its sign leaves a valid uniform chirotope; (2) set deg(i) = #mutable bases containing i and m2(i,j) = #mutable bases containing both i and j; (3) colour the ground set by col_0(i) = deg(i), then refine at most 3 times by col_{t+1}(i) = rank of (col_t(i), sorted multiset over j != i of (m2(i,j), col_t(j))) among the n composite values, ranks assigned by ascending sort, stopping early if the number of distinct colours did not grow (the assignment is kept, then the loop stops); (4) order the colour classes by (class size ascending, colour rank ascending) and let them occupy the positions 1..n in that order; (5) the key is the MAXIMUM, over all relabellings sending each colour class onto its designated block of positions and over all of {0,1}^n x {0,1}, of the resulting key integer.  Because the colouring is invariant under reorientation and global negation and equivariant under relabelling, this is a well-defined function of the G'-orbit, so distinct keys certify distinct classes.  The unrestricted maximum over all of S_n would be a cleaner convention but costs about 1.5 s per class, i.e. some 160 CPU-days here.
conventions.stab_semantics: stab[i] = 2^kappa * #{relabellings in the set of step (5) that attain the maximum} = |Stab_{G'}(chi)|.

array_sha256_note: SHA-256 of the raw little-endian C-contiguous buffer of each array (numpy .tobytes()), so the hashes survive repacking of the .npz container.

witness.purpose: a mutation SPANNING TREE over the same rows: it certifies REACHABILITY, i.e. that all listed classes lie in ONE connected component of the mutation graph on classes.  The coverage array alone certifies the catalog (valid, pairwise inequivalent, exact stabilizers, right mass); it says nothing about how the classes are joined to each other.
witness.indexing: row i of every witness array refers to row i of coverage_4_9.npz, i.e. to the class with key key_hi[i]*2^64 + key_lo[i].

arrays.parent: int32; the row this class was reached from, -1 at the unique root
arrays.flip: uint8; colex index of the mutated basis (0..M-1)
arrays.sigma: uint8 (N,n); a permutation of 1..n, sigma[i][x-1] = sigma(x)
arrays.eps: uint16; reorientation bitmask, bit (x-1) set iff element x is reoriented
arrays.gsgn: uint8; the global sign s in {0,1}
arrays.depth: uint16; distance from row i to the root along parent pointers

witness.identity: for every non-root row i, with chi_i the chirotope decoded from key i, B_j the j-th basis in colex order and mu_B the sign flip on B, EXACTLY: (sigma[i], eps[i], gsgn[i]) . chi_i = mu_{B_flip[i]} ( chi_parent[i] ), the group acting as recorded under conventions.group.  Equivalently, the recorded element is the VOLTAGE of the mutation edge parent[i] -> i.
witness.why_this_certifies_reachability: the identity exhibits mu_{B_flip[i]}(chi_parent[i]) as a G'-translate of chi_i, hence (i) B_flip[i] really is a mutable basis of chi_parent[i] -- the mutant is valid because chi_i is valid and G' preserves validity -- and (ii) rows parent[i] and i are adjacent in the mutation graph on G'-classes.  depth[root]=0 with depth[i]=depth[parent[i]]+1 makes the parent map strictly depth-decreasing, so it is acyclic and every row reaches the unique root.  Therefore all 9276595 listed classes lie in one connected component.
witness.root_sentinels: at the root, parent=-1, flip=0, sigma=identity, eps=0, gsgn=0, depth=0; the identity is not asserted there.

how_to_obtain: coverage_4_9.npz (62.2 MB) and witness_4_9.npz (83.5 MB) are NOT tracked in git (see .gitignore); this MANIFEST.json is.  No archived release exists yet -- one is planned, and until it does the only way to obtain the arrays is to REGENERATE them: run `python runbig.py 4 9 <workers>` (about 4 h on 4 cores; it writes data/big_4_9/level_*.npz), then `python export_coverage.py 4 9 data/big_4_9 data/coverage_4_9`.  The array_sha256 / witness_array_sha256 values below pin the result: they are SHA-256 of the raw array buffers, so they must reproduce exactly, whereas the .npz file hashes need not in general (the zip container may record timestamps).
